title: Note Circle, Sharps, Flats, and Enharmonic Equivalents — Beginner Guitar Theory
summary: JustinGuitar’s lesson introduces the note circle (the chromatic twelve-note system), the concept of octaves as duplicates across the fretboard, and the basic wiring of natural notes (A–G) with sharps and flats. The video defines enharmonic equivalents (notes that sound the same but have different names, such as A# and Bb), explains semitone and tone (whole-step) as steps around the note circle, and uses practical guitar references (e.g., the 12th fret octave cue and the 5th-fret A example) to map semitone movement to frets. It also covers why some intervals do not have sharps/flats between certain pairs of notes (B–C and E–F) and how spellings like B#, Cb, E#, and F can be equivalent to other notes. The content is framed as foundational music theory for beginners and as a precursor to more advanced theory later in the course.
